content: Melvin-Koushki sums up that Ibn Turka's presentation of lettrism as the defining science of a new age is part of a grander doctrine of the upward evolution of humanity, conceived and actualized through a neoplatonic-lettrist-hermetic theory and praxis. He sees the actualization of the prophetic legacy, mediated by the Imams and the ancients, as effected through Akhlāṭī's teachings and his own writings and those of his students and peers, men of might and vision; he upholds prisca sapientia and at the same time insists on an unprecedented and millenarian doctrine of progress.
